VERDICT: the pilot feeds the skill, and the concern is refuted on the numbers but correctly aimed.

1. 40 skill_rules → 35 distinct (5 merges). 20 NEW / 15 OVERLAP (8 sharpened) / 1 CONTRADICTS. NEW = 57%, clustered exactly where git is blind (fixtures+tooling 4/5, working discipline 6/7, spec style 3/3); test-doubles/layers came back 0/3 NEW with `row_stub(**overrides)` reproduced near-verbatim — miner validation, not a null result.
2. 39 failure_modes → 30 TIMELESS / 8 2025-ERA / 1 HARNESS-SOLVED. Per file: day-019 = 17/1/1, day-016 = 13/7/0. Seven of the eight parked entries are Gemini, six after its silent flash downgrade — a model artifact, not an era artifact.
3. 11 of 35 rules are `needed-enforcement` (the C3 candidates); 11 of 35 currently have no detector or rubric item (unfalsifiable prose, flagged); ~11 T1 / ~9 T2 / ~7 T3 detectors implied.
4. Two defects to fix in schema: mined rule G5 prescribes `git add -p`, which the same file records failing from a non-interactive tool (needs a `feasibility:` check); and neither day yields a commit-after-RED rule though canonical calls it the keystone, which v1 cannot distinguish from oversight.
5. Schema v2 needs: `philosophy:` section (the `because:` clauses carried the whole WHY layer by accident), `rule_id:`/`tests_rule:` linkage, `overlap:` + canonical §ref computed at mine time, `era_class:` plus file-level `model:` with sub-session boundaries, mandatory `rule_origin:` (missing on 10 of 39), and a `gap:` negative-space field.
